title: "You sound bad" fixes
idea: Most bad-audio reports come down to how you talk into the mic: too loud, too close, or too much gain. Being off frequency or in a bad spot can do it too.

rows: FM audio drops out on voice peaks
Talking too loudly. Talk more quietly
Too loud or too close. Talk farther away from the mic
Off frequency, too loud or too close, or a bad location. Check all three
Too much mic gain. Turn it down
Your signal is getting into the mic cable. Clip a ferrite choke onto it

pairs: FM audio drops out on voice peaks
An FM station is slightly off frequency
Your signal feeds back into the mic cable
Off frequency, too loud, or a bad spot

compare.how: Too much audio. Back away from the mic.
Distorted audio. Turn the gain down.
The audio sounds distorted, not higher or lower in pitch.

traps.wrong: Your FM deviation is too low
traps.why: Low deviation makes you quiet. Dropouts on voice peaks come from talking too loudly.
Mic gain affects your audio, not the antenna match. Too much gives distorted audio.
The pitch doesn't change. FM received slightly off frequency sounds distorted.
Louder makes over-deviation worse. Talk farther away from the mic.

traps.wrong: You are speaking too loudly or too close to the microphone
traps.why: Speaking too loudly or too close is one cause, but so are being off frequency and a bad location. It's all of them.

traps.wrong: Adding extra feedline to the antenna to lower SWR
traps.why: Extra feedline doesn't fix distortion. A ferrite choke keeps your signal out of the mic cable.
